narrative.overview:
The site is the finishes board a designer lays on the table at the first meeting. Deep green baize felt is the ground of every page. On it sit ivory card-stock tags that carry words, framed prints of the studio's own finished rooms, and real material chips cropped from those photographs. Brass is the hardware: pins, engraved promise plates, and every action.

Composition is pinned, not gridded-flat: objects sit slightly off-axis, overlap, and step down the board at staggered heights. The deep green and gold of the brand are load-bearing; the board is warm and tactile, never cold.

Motion follows the physics of the board: the hero print drops, pins press, the caption tag swings; a chosen product lifts with a brass glow while its thumbnail flies into the quote plate.
keyCharacteristics: Felt-textured green baize ground with a top-left light pool
Ivory tags for all reading text
Brass reserved for pins, promise plates, actions and the chosen state
Real material chips as category controls
Small tilts, overlaps and staggered heights on one 12-column board

rules.name: The Hardware Rule
rules.body: Brass appears only as pins, plates that carry a promise or action, and the ring of a chosen piece.

rules.name: The Two-Text-Colours Rule
rules.body: Ink on Ivory for body; on baize, Ivory headings and Moss supporting lines.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Days, phone numbers, quantities, request and step numbers use tabular figures.

rules.name: The One Pen Rule
rules.body: The hand face writes one caption on the focal print only.

rules.name: The Board Rule
rules.body: Never three equal cards on one baseline; vary span or vertical offset.

rules.name: The Felt Rule
rules.body: Shadows fall downward and blur into the felt; elevation changes by lifting, never by borders.

dos: Do keep baize as the ground of every public page and put reading text on ivory tags.
Do use real material crops from the studio's own photographs for chips, with provenance recorded.
Do make every primary action a Brass Plate and every promise an engraved plate.
Do tilt and stagger board objects at md/lg and straighten them on hover.
Do honour reduced motion by removing spatial movement while keeping state feedback.
donts: Don't fill brass flat or use it as a decorative heading colour, border or band.
Don't introduce white or grey page surfaces; the only white is the translucent field well inside a tag.
Don't use stock or generated imagery for rooms or materials.
Don't set body copy directly on baize beyond short Moss ledes and captions.
Don't use the hand face anywhere but a single caption tag.
